Water at 55000PSi is forced through a 0.012" diamond orifice. Where it is lead through a 0.035" Tungsten carbide nozzle, the part in the picture coming from the top, and fine sand is introduced just before the nozzle.
The sand does the actual cutting.
Material being cut is Stainless Steel.

Stick your finger in there.

Quick question. Are there any health risks to this? I'm sure people are assuming the water keeps everything in check, but sand being blasted that hard to rip through steel must be getting crushed into ultra fine particles. The kind of stuff that likes to get into your lungs and never leave. And once the water evaporates you're basically in the same situation.

The plate to be cut sits on a grid of steel which sits in water. All the steel and sand particles are contained in the water tank. We rinse off the plate after cutting to wash off the mud.
